1627465fd64e8d6e: Working in tech can produce a catalog of woes, and each Monday The Register shares yours in "Who, Me?" – our reader-contributed column chronicling tech-related mistakes, heartaches, and back-breaks. This week, meet an Italian reader we'll Regomize as "Marco," who took us back to what he called "The Roaring Nineties, when big computer companies sold pretty much everything, from graphics workstations to enterprise laser printers." They sold it all through hefty paper catalogs, because this was before broadband and Marco's company had only a 19k baud dial-up connection. Marco's boss, whom he described as a "sciagurato" – Italian for a wretch – kept one of those catalogs on his desk. "He perused it every day, like a kid waiting for Christmas," Marco told The Register. "One day he found an exceptional laser printer at almost one-seventh the cost. It was such a good a deal he ordered two of them." Marco said the boss told anyone who would listen that this feat of cost-cutting would surely propel him out of the tech team and into management. "The wiser among us were already counting the days until the disaster," Marco wrote. Disaster duly arrived with the delivery. "When the courier delivered the printer, it came in two huge packages, but not big enough for a laser printer," Marco observed. After wrestling with the packaging, the horrible truth emerged. "Our boss had bought two laser printer stands," Marco wrote, "because the catalog showed the stands with the printer on top." The company therefore had two stands and no printers. The boss's claim to promotion-worthy procurement prowess had collapsed. "We promptly hid the two pieces of junk in the darkness of our 'obsolete hardware store' and they are probably still there," Marco wrote. He suspects they are not alone, but surrounded by "other good deals, all waiting for the mercy of incineration." Have you or a colleague ordered the wrong thing? If so, click here to send your story to Who, Me? We'll put it on display rather than hide it in the back room. ®
1ba353e57acde6c6: AMPANG JAYA: "It was like a massive wave suddenly crashing in."
That was how a resident of Jalan Kolam Air Lama described the flash flood that saw waters surge to waist level in under two minutes during a downpour yesterday afternoon.
Thiyaga Rajan Shanmugam, in his 40s, said torrential rain began around 3.30pm with water rising swiftly around 4pm.
The flash flood inundated his house and 11 other residential units along Lorong Kolam Ayer Lama A, damaging property.
"The water swept in from above like a giant wave, flowing at an extremely fast pace. I only managed to save my car, but all the furniture and electrical appliances inside the house were ruined.
"I only moved in four months ago after buying and renovating the place earlier this year. Everything was brand new. Now, it's all gone," he told reporters at his home.
Thiyaga estimated his losses at over RM100,000, including the cost of replacing electrical items and furniture, and repainting damaged walls.
He said that the waters subsided around 5.30pm as the rain abated, adding that it was the worst flooding he had ever experienced.
He also claimed that fallen timber left uncollected in the surrounding area may have choked the natural drainage flow.
"Officers from the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ) arrived shortly after to assist.
"MPAJ helped clear the debris off the roads and dispatched contractors to unclog the drains while residents cleaned up their homes," he said.
Another resident, Nazrul Afiq, also in his 40s, said he was shocked by how rapidly the water level rose, noting that previous flash floods in the area never reached such heights.
"Water rushed inside and even damaged sturdy structures like wall barriers and front fences. This is the first time I witnessed water levels this high. It was completely unexpected.
"It flooded here last year, but nothing like this," Nazrul said.

Nazrul said that based on his observation, two nearby floodgates play a crucial role in managing the area's drainage system. He said that water currents in the main drains remain unusually swift even during dry spells.
He said that during downpours, strong back pressure causes the drains to overflow and backup rapidly into the neighbourhood.

"Some neighbours checked the upstream drainage area and found felled trees and timber that were never cleared properly. This debris blocked the main drains and contributed heavily to the flood," he claimed.
Nazrul also saw how a driver attempted to navigate through the rising waters.
"I saw a Perodua Axia driven by a woman almost get swept away as she tried to drive out of our lane. The car became completely stranded in the middle of the road.

"Fortunately, she survived unhurt after the rain stopped and the water began to recede. But we cannot afford to let this happen again. It poses a direct threat to the lives of residents and the public," he said, urging local authorities to take swift corrective action.
In a related incident, floodwaters also caused a nearby school's perimeter wall to collapse.

ae05eee7520c7091: NAGOYA: A sport once banned in much of the United States and famously decried as "human cockfighting" by a high-profile politician is making an ambitious play for the Olympics.
Mixed Martial Arts, better known as MMA, is making its Asian Games debut this week in Japan – a milestone that fighters and organisers hope will one day lead to an even bigger prize.
Galastein Tan, director general of the Federation of International Mixed Martial Arts, said being at the Asian Games was "a big step."
"As for any sport, the inclusion in the continental games is critical," he told AFP in Nagoya.

"Obviously the inclusion means that you already have a good governance structure, you have enough members, athletes to be able to compete, your ruleset, your officials are ready and therefore it is a significant one."
At a compact gym akin to a school sports hall, men and women scrap it out in separate categories in front of a modest but enthusiastic crowd.
Many of the competitors are from countries with proud histories in fighting sports – Thailand, Kazakhstan, the Philippines and hosts Japan to name a few.
Inspiring a generation
For fans of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), the MMA promoter synonymous with the sport, there is one immediate difference.
In UFC, which in June held an event on the South Lawn of the White House, the rough and tumble takes place inside a caged octagon.
At the Asian Games competitors do battle on a white and grey mat, but they are not fenced in.
For martial artists used to fighting in a cage, this takes some adapting to – a fence "does not really align with Olympic values", said Tan.
Getting everyone to agree on the rules of the competition, including what moves are allowed, is one major obstacle to MMA being at the Olympics.
Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon, who is guaranteed to win at least a silver medal, said that Asian Games and Olympic recognition will encourage a generation to take up the sport.
"I think it will grow the talent pool a lot," she said.
"It will encourage more children and teenagers to take up the sport and take it seriously.
"Because now there's a clear pathway, right? You can join a national team, the next step you can go to the Olympics."
'We are ready'
MMA is not the only sport debuting at Asia's premier sporting event and hoping one day to get into the Olympics.
So too is teqball – roughly a crossover between football and table tennis – and there is also the fast-growing racquet sport of padel.
It makes for a crowded field, and there are many other sports with Olympic ambitions.
Plenty of hard work and political lobbying lies ahead if MMA is to make it.
"We have been in talks with the IOC and other relevant stakeholders that have influence or decision on the recognition," said an upbeat Tan.
The sport does have Dana White in its corner – the UFC chief is openly supportive of Olympic inclusion.
Of the other issues on the long path to Olympic recognition there is a perception in the eyes of some that MMA is too violent.
Still, driven by the phenomenal success of the UFC, MMA is now mainstream – a far cry from the 1990s when US senator John McCain likened the early version of the sport to cockfighting.
Getting the whole of MMA to coalesce around one governing body is also essential if an Olympic place is to one day come.
Los Angeles in 2028 is too soon, and then comes Brisbane four years later.
"Nothing is impossible," said Tan.
"We hope that MMA is a sport that the Olympics finds relevance to and the ability to connect with both adults and also the youth.
"(It is) a sport which has global appeal and a sport that is ready and capable of fitting into a major Games schedule.
"So if the IOC or LA28 comes and say, MMA, would you like to be in as a medal sport or demo sport, we are ready." - AFP

90d6b8aaff0e9643: PHILADELPHIA: An emotional Ed Sheeran broke down in tears on stage during his first concert following a chaotic week that saw all of his supporting acts walk off his tour.
The controversy started when rapper Macklemore was removed from the English singer-songwriter's Loop Tour over on-stage pro-Palestine remarks.
The decision—reportedly driven by pressure from stadium owners like New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft—led to a domino effect.
All remaining opening acts and Sheeran's backing band pulled out in solidarity, leaving the 35-year-old pop star to perform entirely alone.

Opening the show at Lincoln Financial Field Stadium in Philadelphia, Sheeran read a statement from a teleprompter addressing the conflict and his concerns over stadium owners controlling what artistes can say on stage.

"I've had to make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so, so sorry. I don't want to disappoint fans, and I've never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet," Sheeran told the crowd. He stressed that his gigs remain a space where "everyone is welcome," before later apologising to parents in attendance for starting the night with heavy politics rather than music.
By the end of the night, the weight of the moment caught up with him.
Seated on the floor with his face in his hands, a visibly shaken Sheeran wept as the audience cheered in support.
"Thank you. The world is a scary place right now; America is a scary place right now; this gives hope," he said through tears.
Public reaction to Sheeran remains split.
Critics have accused him of fence-sitting, while loyal fans argue the backlash is unfair and should be aimed at corporate venue owners instead.
Sheeran is set to complete nine remaining US tour dates before heading to South America.
3fe1bb81f492732b: PUTRAJAYA: Purata gaji dan upah bulanan warganegara Malaysia meningkat 4.1% kepada RM3,803 pada 2025 berbanding RM3,652 pada tahun sebelumnya, menurut Laporan Survei Gaji dan Upah Malaysia 2025 diterbitkan Jabatan Perangkaan (DOSM) hari ini.
Pada masa sama, penengah gaji dan upah bulanan meningkat 5.3% kepada RM2,940 daripada RM2,793 pada 2024.

DOSM dalam kenyataan hari ini memaklumkan bilangan penerima gaji dan upah bulanan keseluruhan meningkat kepada 12.01 juta orang berbanding 11.96 juta pada 2024 dan daripada jumlah itu, warganegara Malaysia merangkumi 10.38 juta orang atau 86.4% daripada keseluruhan pekerja bergaji sepenuh masa.
“Sektor perkhidmatan mewakili 71.5% menjadi penyumbang utama kepada peningkatan bilangan penerima upah, meningkat 1.8% kepada 7.42 juta orang.

“Sementara itu, perlombongan dan pengkuarian kekal sebagai purata gaji dan upah bulanan tertinggi, iaitu RM6,175 diikuti oleh perkhidmatan (RM3,993), pembuatan (RM3,357), pembinaan (RM3,188) dan pertanian (RM2,575),” menurut kenyataan itu.

Dari segi kemahiran, DOSM memaklumkan pekerja mahir yang merangkumi 36.6% daripada keseluruhan penerima gaji mencatatkan purata gaji dan upah bulanan tertinggi sebanyak RM5,799 berbanding RM5,582 pada 2024.

Kategori separuh mahir yang merangkumi 55.6% daripada penerima gaji pula mencatatkan peningkatan purata gaji sebanyak 4.2% kepada RM2,714 daripada RM2,604 manakala kategori berkemahiran rendah naik 2.6% kepada RM2,184 daripada RM2,128.
“Selangor mencatatkan peratus sumbangan penerima gaji tertinggi iaitu 25.6% daripada jumlah keseluruhan pekerja bergaji warganegara diikuti Johor (13.6%) dan Sarawak (7.6%),” menurut kenyataan itu.

DOSM memaklumkan lima negeri menunjukkan nilai purata gaji dan upah bulanan melebihi paras nasional, iaitu Wilayah Persekutuan Putrajaya pada RM5,417, Kuala Lumpur (RM4,955), Selangor (RM4,258), Pulau Pinang (RM3,912) dan Labuan (RM3,887).
Menurut DOSM, pertumbuhan positif purata dan penengah gaji serta upah bulanan pada 2025 mencerminkan perkembangan lebih baik dalam pasaran buruh dan pendapatan pekerja.

“Menuju ke hadapan, usaha berterusan untuk meningkatkan produktiviti, memperkukuh kemahiran dan mewujudkan pekerjaan bernilai tinggi adalah penting bagi menyokong pertumbuhan gaji benar yang mampan serta kesejahteraan pekerja.

“Selaras dengan aspirasi Rancangan Malaysia Ketiga Belas (RMK13), pembangunan tenaga buruh yang berdaya saing dan produktif serta pengukuhan reformasi pasaran buruh penting bagi menyokong pertumbuhan gaji yang mampan dan inklusif,” menurut kenyataan itu.

1c21ab2912d79953: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Unity Ministry will seek RM550.7 million under Budget 2027 to implement six key programmes aimed at nation-building.
Its minister, Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, said the request would be discussed with the Finance Minister tomorrow.
He said that all six initiatives would focus on fostering a shared national identity, while strengthening unity and harmony in Malaysia.

The initiatives are National Unity and Identity, Community Harmony, Ini Warisan Kita (This Is Our Heritage), Digitalisation of National Treasures, upgrading unity-related premises and matching grants for museums, archives and libraries.

"All requests for allocations under the 2027 Budget will be aligned with the ministry's nation-building agenda, with emphasis on developing a shared identity and strengthening national unity and harmony," he told reporters after launching the Malaysia Storytelling Festival (FPM) 2026 at the National Library today.

Aaron said programmes under the National Unity and Identity initiative would include Gerak Integrasi Perpaduan (GRIP Madani), the Rukun Negara Youth Tour, Jalinan Integrasi Nasional (National Integration Network), Citra Nusa Muzium, museum exhibitions, Semarak Advokasi Arkib, Nadi Budaya Ilmu, and the Digital Library Conference.
Under the Community Harmony initiative, the ministry plans to implement the Progressive Kawasan Rukun Tetangga (KRT) and Community Mediator programmes.
The proposed allocation would also cover the upgrading of unity-related facilities, including Unity Kindergartens (Tabika Perpaduan), archives and village libraries.
"We have 506 village libraries nationwide, as well as 10 memorials and 22 museums under the Museums Department.

The 2027 Budget application includes funding to digitalise the facilities and collections managed by these three agencies. These are the six areas for which we will be seeking funding next year," he said.

On the 2026 Budget, Aaron said the ministry received RM136 million, comprising RM55 million each for KRT and Unity activities, RM20 million for upgrading Unity Kindergartens, RM5 million for museum matching grants and RM1 million for Siamese ethnic culture.
In addition, the ministry was allocated RM650.48 million for operating expenditure and RM117.52 million for development expenditure.
Aaron said the ministry planned to implement various programmes next year, although their execution would depend on the allocation approved under the 2027 Budget.
acf0dfcbd44e7f0b: IPOH, Sept 21 — The next of kin of two victims killed in a road crash on Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here on Saturday are eligible for benefits under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam Scheme for Non-Occupational Accidents.
Perkeso said in a statement today that the victims were Muhammad Izdihar Rafiq Sarajil Korin and Muhamad Faiz Danial Jumri, both aged 19.
Its records showed that Muhammad Izdihar began contributing to Perkeso after starting work in January this year, while Muhamad Faiz had been contributing since August last year.
“Although the accident occurred outside working hours, the next of kin, including the victims’ parents and siblings who may previously have depended on them, remain protected.

“This is the true purpose of Lindung 24 Jam, which provides protection for accidents occurring outside working hours, even when workers have only recently started contributing to Perkeso,” the statement said.

According to Perkeso, the next of kin of Muhammad Izdihar are eligible for Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM945, distributed according to their respective shares, with his parents receiving the payments for life and his three siblings receiving them until they turn 21 or complete a degree.

For Muhamad Faiz, Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM891, distributed according to the respective shares, will be paid to his parents for life, while one sibling will receive the benefit until turning 21 or completing a degree.
In addition, the next of kin of both victims are eligible for a Funeral Management Benefit of RM3,000 each as a one-off payment.
Perkeso said the total periodic pension payments through the Dependants’ Benefit over 15 years to the victims’ next of kin would amount to more than RM275,000.

The crash, which occurred at about 3.35am on Sept 19, killed three male motorcyclists aged between 19 and 20 at the scene, while nine other male motorcyclists aged between 19 and 25 sustained various injuries. — Bernama
bdbc5efb43ccba78: PETALING JAYA: Sabah's power supply network has improved significantly since the state took over regulatory control for electricity and renewable energy in 2024, chief minister Hajiji Noor says.

"Previously, we had to wait four to five years to get our applications approved by the federal Energy Commission, but since we took over, we can get it done ourselves and improve our electricity supply system faster," he said after chairing the Sabah Energy Council meeting in Kota Kinabalu.
Hajiji also said Sabah’s generation reserve is expected to reach 26% by year end. It increased from 8% in 2024 to 19% as of August this year, he said.
He said the System Average Interruption Duration Index also improved from 598 minutes in 2023 to 226 minutes as of July this year.
He attributed these improvements to ongoing initiatives to enhance the grid system.
In 2024, Hajiji said the state’s power supply issues were largely the result of increased demand from investors and businesses opening up in the state.
He said initiatives to strengthen Sabah’s energy sector must be comprehensive, including ensuring reliable transmission and distribution infrastructure.
21f0764e19194039: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 —Bursa Malaysia’s key index rebounded to close the morning session 0.31 per cent higher, paring earlier losses on persistent buying in heavyweights, particularly banking stocks.
At 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.24 points to 1,670.80 from Friday’s close of 1,665.56.
The benchmark index, which opened 1.36 points lower at 1,664.20, moved between 1,661.22 and 1,673.25 during the session.
However, market breadth was negative with losers outnumbering gainers 532 to 480. A total of 491 counters were unchanged, 1,379 untraded and 20 suspended.
Turnover stood at 1.97 billion units worth RM1.26 billion.

In a note today, Apex Securities Bhd said the recent correction on the domestic front has brought valuations to more attractive levels, potentially encouraging bargain hunting and selective buying in blue-chip counters.
“We also expect investors to favour sectors with resilient earnings and stronger domestic or commodity-linked exposure amid the uncertain external environment,” the stockbroking firm said.

Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose eight sen to RM10.40, Public Bank added three sen to RM4.80, CIMB firmed seven sen to RM7.70, and Tenaga Nasional expanded two sen to RM13.06, while IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.63.

As for the most active stocks, Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to 20.5 sen, Jaks Resources gained 1.5 sen to 17 sen, FSBM increased 3.5 sen to 10 sen, AirAsia edged up one sen to 54 sen, and Ni Hsin was flat at 39 sen.

Among the top gainers, Solarvest surged 39 sen to RM3.72, YTL Power strengthened 36 sen to RM5.94, Samaiden jumped 25 sen to RM2.20, Hong Leong Bank added 24 sen to RM22.78, and Ranhill Utilities racked up 21 sen to RM3.12.

Of the top losers, Malaysian Pacific Industries erased 80 sen to RM42, Nestle was 58 sen lower at RM89.00, Time Dotcom dropped 47 sen to RM5.94, Sunway Construction reduced 46 sen to RM7.42, and QL Resources lost 31 sen to RM3.88.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index notched up 0.27 of a point to 12,411.99, while the FBM Top 100 Index slipped 0.16 of a point to 12,210.21.
Meanwhile, the FBM Mid 70 Index contracted 161.52 points to 17,682.50, the FBM Emas Shariah Index shrank 71.08 points to 12,240.91, and the FBM ACE Index advanced 47.14 points to 5,291.74.
Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index trimmed 1.35 points to 183.89, while the Energy Index improved 8.41 points to 829.03.
The Financial Services Index climbed 97.27 points to 19,509.90, while the Plantation Index slid 52.96 points to 9,443.48. — Bernama
e2bec03ae656f3cc: GIFU: Veteran striker Faizal Saari wants Malaysia to maintain their winning momentum as the Speedy Tigers target top spot in Group B of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games men's hockey competition.
Faizal starred with a hat-trick as Malaysia thrashed Uzbekistan 7-0 at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium yesterday, giving the national side a flying start to their campaign.
However, the 35-year-old was quick to focus on Malaysia's second group match against Oman tomorrow.
"I am happy that we managed to get three points from our first match.
"Unfortunately, we started a little slowly, but after that we recovered and kept scoring until we finished with seven goals.
"This result is important because goal difference could play a part at the end of the group stage," said Faizal.
On his hat-trick, Faizal said he was merely looking to make the most of every opportunity to help the team secure victory.
After facing Oman, the Speedy Tigers continue their Group B campaign against Thailand on Thursday before taking on Pakistan on Sept 26 and China on Sept 28.
Malaysia are aiming to finish top of Group B to avoid a likely semi-final clash against Group A champions India.
"We will try to finish the group stage in first place.
"We will take it one match at a time and not look too far ahead because anything can happen in this tournament," said Faizal.
ca12ab55de8c793d: KUALA LUMPUR: S P Setia Bhd is stepping up its presence in northern Penang, almost a decade after acquiring more than 684 hectares in Bertam, Kepala Batas, with the launch of a new public park aimed at strengthening the appeal of its Setia Fontaines township.

The developer has launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park, a 40.5-hectare recreational and community space within the township, as it seeks to deepen the development's role as a destination for residents and visitors in Seberang Perai Utara.

The park forms part of S P Setia's broader placemaking strategy, which includes a 25.5-hectare man-made lake and musical fountain, designed to provide recreational, wellness and community spaces within the township.

Penang State Executive Councillor for Tourism and Creative Economy Wong Hon Wai said the development could contribute to the broader socio-economic growth of Kepala Batas and the northern Seberang Perai region.

He said the initiative demonstrated the role of private-sector investment in creating sustainable communities, strengthening local economies and supporting Penang's longer-term development objectives.

The effort not only enhances the value and appeal of Setia Fontaines as a premier township development but also contributes meaningfully to the broader socio-economic growth and development of Kepala Batas and the Northern Seberang Perai region, Wong said.
The launch was attended by Tun Ramli Ngah Talib, Toh Puan Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, residents and members of the public.

S P Setia president and chief executive officer Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the launch underscored the company's long-term commitment to Penang and its approach of developing townships around community, public spaces and shared experiences.

"Setia Fontaines Heritage Park represents our continued commitment to building beyond homes. Through thoughtful placemaking, green public spaces and community-led experiences, we are shaping Setia Fontaines into an integrated township that contributes to Penang's growth while creating long-term value for residents, visitors and the wider community," he said.

Zaini said the Heritage Park is envisioned as more than a township amenity but as a new lifestyle and recreational attraction with the potential to support visitation, public engagement and destination appeal for Seberang Perai Utara and the wider northern region.

The launch was accompanied by the Jom Mai Setia Fontaines Carnival, featuring family and community activities, Malaysia Day programmes, cultural and entertainment performances, as well as tourism-related activations.

The programme was supported by strategic collaborations with Tourism Malaysia, Penang Global Tourism, Maybank and other partners, reinforcing the developer's efforts to position Setia Fontaines as a broader community and lifestyle destination.
20f227ec05bd0508: SLUG: HKKASTAM
14 Malaysians held in Hong Kong over suspected drug smuggling
Nor Azizah Mokhtar
KUALA LUMPUR: Fourteen Malaysians were arrested by Hong Kong Customs for allegedly smuggling drugs into Hong Kong in the first six months of this year.

While the number may appear small, drug smuggling into a foreign territory is a serious offence, with the largest seizure involving 25kg of ketamine worth HK$9.5 million (RM5.3 million) during the first half of this year.
Hong Kong Customs told BH that the figure was recorded after 24 Malaysians were arrested throughout 2025, six in 2024 and eight in 2023.
The agency said the Malaysian suspects arrested between 2023 and June this year were aged between 20 and 67.
"Among the latest cases involving Malaysians were four arrests in three separate cases at Hong Kong International Airport in July," it said.
On July 9, a 19-year-old Malaysian man was arrested after allegedly carrying about 3kg of cannabis concealed in checked-in luggage upon arriving in Hong Kong from Kuala Lumpur via Singapore.

"On July 16, another 19-year-old Malaysian man was arrested after allegedly carrying about 11kg of cannabis flowers worth HK$2 million (about RM1.1 million) in checked-in luggage when he arrived from Bangkok, Thailand, via Manila, the Philippines," it said.

On July 21, two Malaysian men, aged 22 and 27, were arrested in separate cases after allegedly carrying about 7kg of methamphetamine concealed in packets of drinks in checked-in luggage when they arrived from Bangkok.
Each seizure was estimated to be worth HK$3.5 million (RM2 million).
Most recently, a 33-year-old Malaysian woman was arrested on Sept 12 after she was found allegedly attempting to smuggle 8kg of cannabis buds worth HK$1.6 million (RM830,000) into Hong Kong.
The woman had arrived at Hong Kong International Airport from Bangkok before she was detained during a customs inspection.
Hong Kong Customs reminded the public not to act as mules by carrying controlled goods into or out of Hong Kong.
"They are also reminded not to carry goods for others if they do not know their contents.
"Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, drug trafficking is a serious offence punishable by a maximum fine of HK$5 million (about RM2.8 million) and life imprisonment upon conviction," it said.
Intelligence sharing

Hong Kong Customs said it continued to strengthen cooperation with enforcement and customs agencies in various countries, including Malaysia, through intelligence sharing and enforcement cooperation to combat cross-border drug trafficking.

"We constantly adjust our enforcement strategies and resource deployment according to changing drug trafficking trends, while adopting risk assessment and intelligence-led approaches to detect drug inflows into Hong Kong through various channels.
"Hong Kong Customs will continue to focus on screening passengers from high-risk areas to combat cross-border drug trafficking," it said.
Hong Kong Customs statistics showed 220 drug-related arrests were recorded between January and June this year, involving the seizure of 4,104kg of drugs worth HK$1.488 billion (RM835 million).
Throughout 2025, the agency recorded 416 arrests and seized 7,523kg of drugs worth HK$2.932 billion, compared with 365 arrests involving 6,296kg of drugs worth HK$2.626 billion in 2024.

65f2a8888310940d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Tengku Mahkota of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah Ibni Al-Sultan Abdullah will invest US$552,500 (RM2.3 million) in Nasdaq-listed AI technology company Sagtec Global Ltd through a private placement.
Sagtec said Tengku Hassanal has agreed to subscribe for 850,000 Class A ordinary shares at US$0.65 each.
The placement remains subject to customary closing conditions, including board approval and compliance with securities laws and Nasdaq requirements.
The subscription amount is payable within six months of the share issuance, and early payment is allowed without penalty.
Sagtec said the equity injection will strengthen its financial flexibility without adding borrowings or scheduled interest and principal repayments.

The proceeds will support the development and commercialisation of its AI-assisted software and enterprise technology platforms, cloud and digital infrastructure, enterprise projects, business development and working capital.
The company is also targeting expansion in Malaysia and other Southeast Asian markets.
"Malaysia has the talent and capabilities to develop technology companies that can compete regionally and internationally.
"I believe Sagtec has meaningful potential to contribute to this progress through its work in artificial intelligence, enterprise software and digital infrastructure," Tengku Hassanal said.
"My investment reflects my confidence in the company's direction, management and long-term growth potential," he added.
Sagtec chairman and chief executive officer Ng Chen Lok said the company was "deeply honoured" to welcome Tengku Hassanal as a strategic investor.

"Our priority is to deploy this capital prudently toward initiatives that can generate sustainable revenue, deepen our customer relationships and expand our recurring software and technology-services business," he added.
e51501d8d113d1df: NEW YORK, Sept 21 — US and Chinese economic officials discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns at meetings yesterday as they set the stage for a summit of the countries’ top leaders this week.

The talks come as both powers confront rising fears that increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems could wipe out humanity, offering a rare incentive for cooperation despite an intensifying race for technological supremacy.
“We just had a very successful engagement with the Chinese on trade and AI,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters after long talks with a team led by Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng.
The talks are a prelude to a planned White House meeting on Thursday of the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The discussions, which also included the top US trade official Jamieson Greer, lasted around eight hours at JPMorgan Chase’s headquarters in New York.
Bessant said the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”
“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.
Such notifications are for potential “incidents,” or a situation “that rises up to a national security level from AI,” he said, adding that both sides have agreed to meet again.
Bessent and He also spoke one-on-one during the day, a source familiar with the matter said.
Chinese state media described the meetings as “candid, in-depth, and constructive” today.

“The two sides engaged in… discussions on key economic and trade issues of mutual interest, such as implementing the consensus from previous consultations and promoting bilateral trade and investment,” Xinhua news agency said in a brief readout.
Chinese and US officials also held a dialogue on “issues related to AI”, Xinhua added, without giving any further details.

Chinese official Li Chenggang, who was elevated to a top-level international trade representative post shortly before the meetings, was present in the New York talks too. But the Chinese delegation did not address reporters.
Greer stressed yesterday it is “imperative that we are able to work together.”
Both sides are looking to ease tensions on trade, technology and other strategic concerns. These include the possible extension of a trade truce and guardrails for AI development.
Non-sensitive trade
Asked about the possibility of mutual tariff reduction on certain goods, Greer said teams “are continuing to work through this.”
The aim is to identify “non-sensitive” goods that can be considered separately from trade measures in the future, he added.
Such products could cover consumer goods from the Chinese side and energy, agricultural and other products like medical devices on the US side.
Beyond less sensitive items, US officials are also seeking to ensure the continued flow of rare earth magnets and critical minerals that are vital for US manufacturers.
Working level meetings could continue into today, a source familiar with discussions earlier told AFP.
Previous negotiations saw China pledge purchases of US agriculture goods too, and their fulfilment of the terms could also be an issue under scrutiny.
Another issue is US economic pressure on Iran, as Washington’s war with Tehran has entered its seventh month.
China is a top economic partner of Iran that buys much of its oil output and a key diplomatic backer.
Analysts caution that expectations for the Trump-Xi summit are low.
“One of the only things we can hope for in the short term is a truce, and that this will likely continue through the remainder of this year,” said former US deputy secretary of state Kurt Campbell.
“I think you will hear the president announce the intention to meet with Xi Jinping two more times,” added Campbell, who is now chairman of The Asia Group consultancy.

Trump and Xi are expected to meet in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzhen, China. Trump is also anticipated to invite Xi to the G20 summit in December at his Doral resort in Miami. — AFP

aa3fca2a6802e2b7: TEMERLOH: Seven people believed to belong to three criminal groups involved in stealing cables belonging to utility and telecommunications companies were arrested by police in several raids here between Sept 15 and 19.

District police chief assistant commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police arrested six men and a woman, aged between 16 and 40, and seized various items including cables, vehicles and cable-cutting equipment worth RM50,000.

"Four of those arrested have previous records for criminal and drug-related offences. Urine tests conducted on all the suspects also found that four of them tested positive for methamphetamine," he said at a press conference at the Temerloh district police headquarters today.

He said based on intelligence and interrogation of the seven suspects, police identified three criminal groups involved in stealing Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) cables from June to September this year.

"They are a criminal group known as 'Geng Mat Letrik', comprising two of those arrested. The next group, known as 'Geng Mista', comprises one suspect who was arrested, while the other four arrested were members of 'Geng Sasi'," he said.
Nasyim said police were actively tracking down six men from Geng Mista and Geng Sasi who were still at large and believed to be involved in the thefts.

"All those arrested are currently being remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code, with investigations conducted under Sections 379 and 431A of the Penal Code, as well as Section 235(2) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
"We have completed the interrogation. The remand period ends tomorrow, and we may apply for an extension of the remand order after this," he said.
He said police believed the stolen cables were sold at RM30 per kg to scrap metal dealers, including those within and outside the Temerloh district.
The activity involved not only the theft of metal but also the sabotage of national infrastructure, disruption of essential services and endangerment of public safety.
"Our message to these criminals is simple. You have disrupted the lives of Malaysians, and we will not tolerate it. We will track you down and charge you," he said. — BERNAMA

95b9ea5a7148c70a: KUALA LUMPUR: Che Puan Sarimah Ibrahim has revealed that she turned down a chance to appear in the hit Netflix series Wednesday, choosing to put her religious and personal values before Hollywood fame.

She explained that she had to step away from another shortlisted position for Nine Perfect Strangers, as that role also involved a kissing scene and required her to wear a bikini on camera.
Despite turning down these offers, Sarimah—who signed with London-based talent agency Fiona Cross Management in 2024—remains open to overseas projects if the right role comes along.

0034d87e9d03511b: KUALA TERENGGANU: More than 57,000 illegal immigrants have been detained in 9,700 operations conducted nationwide from Jan 1 to Sept 17, said Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli.

44074492b0d75eb3: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Lucas Wehle and Mona Rasidah will be part of a historic moment when surfing makes its official debut at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with the pair set to test themselves against some of the sport's established names.

The surfing competition will be held from Sept 25-28 at Pacific Long Beach, also known as Akabane Long Beach, in Tahara, and will also serve as an official qualifier for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

For 17-year-old Lucas, the event represents an opportunity to gain experience at the highest level of Asian competition after he helped Malaysia secure the required qualification at last year's Asian Regional Championships in India.
The teenager could find himself up against Japan's Olympic silver medallist Kanoa Igarashi, Connor O'Leary, a top-10 World Surf League surfer, and Indonesia's world junior champion Bronson Meidy.
Rather than feeling pressured by the prospect of competing against surfers he has watched at the Olympics and World Surf League, Lucas said their presence has only fired him up to perform.

"I've been watching these guys compete in the Olympics and the World Surf League among the best in the world, and I look up to them, especially Kanoa Igarashi, who is an idol of mine and who also trains in Portugal like me sometimes," he said.
Lucas has spent the past week training at the competition venue and has experienced a wide range of conditions, from knee-high waves to waves produced by a powerful typhoon swell.
The forecast suggests smaller waves during the opening two days, but Lucas believes his preparation in Portugal and Bali has equipped him to handle the conditions.
"In a heat, the conditions are the same for both competitors, so it's often about who can adapt best," he said.
While Lucas is one of the youngest surfers in the competition, Malaysia also has Mona, 41, providing a striking contrast in experience and generations.
But Lucas does not see their age difference as significant, instead viewing Mona simply as another athlete chasing the best possible performance.

"It's cool to know that age is just a number and that a surfing career can last that long. I'm grateful for the groundwork that previous generations of surfers in Malaysia laid, and I hope I can do the same for future generations," he said.
And while surfing is an individual sport once a heat begins, Lucas said reaching this stage has been a collective effort involving his family, school and coaches in Portugal and Bali.

His school has given him the flexibility to travel for training and competitions, while Malaysian head coach Muttakin Talib, an International Surfing Association (ISA) judge, has helped him prepare through competition simulations and video analysis.
"Once I'm in the water and the heat is on, I'm on my own, but there is a lot that goes on before that, and I wouldn't be here today without the support network I have," said Lucas.
He also credited the National Sports Council and Malaysian Surfing Association for their belief in him as he prepares to experience the Asian Games for the first time.
"I just hope I'll be able to show what I'm capable of and make everyone at home proud," said Lucas.
cdf698b12df61d01: KUALA LUMPUR: There will be no exemptions for senior citizens, B40 group or depositors nearing their turn to perform the haj from the RM15,000 minimum savings requirement to retain their place in the haj queue.
In a response to Berita Harian, Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) said the requirement currently applies to all depositors regardless of age, income group or position in the haj queue.
However, the requirement will not take effect immediately as existing depositors are given a transition period until Dec 31, 2028, to gradually build their savings to RM15,000.
"At present, there are no specific exemptions based on age, income group or position in the queue.
"The RM15,000 minimum savings requirement applies to all depositors who wish to retain their eligibility in the haj queue," TH responded.
It added that the RM15,000 threshold was not a measure of whether a person was wealthy, but a benchmark to determine a prospective pilgrim's basic financial readiness.
The amount also takes into account the current haj payment rate for the B40 group and is aimed at encouraging depositors to prepare financially earlier and gradually.
TH said the main principle behind the requirement was to ensure depositors had at least a minimum level of financial readiness when their turn came to receive a haj offer.

The move is also aimed at ensuring the limited haj quota is fully utilised and reducing instances where offers have to be deferred or given to other depositors because prospective pilgrims are not financially ready.
"The aim is not to differentiate between those who are better off, but to ensure every prospective pilgrim has the same basic level of readiness when their turn comes to perform the haj," TH said.
It said the need to increase savings has become more pressing as more than 80 per cent of about 4.1 million depositors registered for the haj have savings of less than RM15,000.
TH also said 53 per cent of its 9.8 million depositors had savings of less than RM1,300, indicating a significant gap between haj registration and financial readiness to perform the pilgrimage.
TH encouraged depositors to begin preparing early, save consistently and build their financial capacity according to their means.
Depositors already in the haj queue have until Dec 31, 2028, to gradually reach the RM15,000 threshold before the new eligibility mechanism takes effect in 2029.
The RM15,000 minimum savings requirement is part of TH's Seruan Istito'ah approach, which emphasises financial readiness before performing the haj.

The approach was intended to make the haj queue more orderly and ensure prospective pilgrims were financially prepared to accept an offer when their turn came, while reducing the number of offers that had to be deferred because of financial constraints.
Previously, TH said the RM15,000 threshold was not necessarily permanent and could be reviewed if there were significant changes in the cost of performing the haj or other related factors.
16b7e82ad32bd0a2: PUTRAJAYA: The average monthly salary and wage of Malaysians increased by 4.1 per cent to RM3,803 in 2025, compared with RM3,652 the previous year, according to the Salaries and Wages Survey Report 2025 published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
At the same time, the median monthly salary and wage increased by 5.3 per cent to RM2,940 from RM2,793 in 2024.

It said the total number of monthly salary and wage earners rose to 12.01 million, up from 11.96 million in 2024, adding that, of the total, Malaysians accounted for 10.38 million, or 86.4 per cent of all full-time paid employees.

"The services sector, which represents 71.5 per cent, was the main contributor to the increase in the number of wage earners, rising by 1.8 per cent to 7.42 million people. Meanwhile, mining and quarrying remained the highest average monthly salary and wage at RM6,175, followed by services (RM3,993), manufacturing (RM3,357), construction (RM3,188) and agriculture (RM2,575)," DOSM said in a statement today.
In terms of skills, DOSM said skilled workers, who accounted for 36.6 per cent of all salary earners, recorded the highest average monthly salary and wage at RM5,799, compared with RM5,582 in 2024.

Meanwhile, the semi-skilled category, which accounted for 55.6 per cent of salary earners, recorded a 4.2 per cent increase in average salary to RM2,714 from RM2,604, while the low-skilled category rose by 2.6 per cent to RM2,184 from RM2,128.
"Selangor recorded the highest share of salary earners, at 25.6 per cent of the total number of paid Malaysian workers, followed by Johor (13.6 per cent) and Sarawak (7.6 per cent)," it added.

The DOSM said five states recorded average monthly salaries and wages above the national level, namely Putrajaya at RM5,417, Kuala Lumpur (RM4,955), Selangor (RM4,258), Penang (RM3,912) and Labuan (RM3,887).
It said the positive growth in average and median monthly salaries and wages in 2025 reflects improved labour market conditions and workers' incomes.
"Looking ahead, continued efforts to increase productivity, strengthen skills and create high-value jobs are important to support sustainable real wage growth and workers' well-being.

"In line with the aspirations of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), developing a competitive and productive workforce and strengthening labour market reforms are important to support sustainable and inclusive wage growth," it added.

ae6e58ddeed0c3bb: MELAKA: Pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN) Melaka Ab Rauf Yusoh mengingatkan pihak yang mahu bekerjasama dengan partinya pada PRN tidak merundingkan perkara itu menerusi media sosial.

de01e709f369dc0c: MARSEILLE: The alarm bells are ringing at Olympique de Marseille after a run of poor results left them floundering near the foot of Ligue 1, with a loss of form following on from financial restrictions imposed before the start of the season.
Marseille were beaten for a fifth successive match when they went down 2-1 to arch rivals Paris St Germain at home on Sunday and sit second from bottom in the French top flight.
The club could not reinforce their squad before the start of the season after a spending handbrake imposed by both Uefa and French football’s financial watchdog.
Record losses meant cutting their wage bill and letting players go, but Marseille were not expected to struggle as much as they have in recent weeks.

“We can suffer defeats, that's part of football, but being satisfied with honourable defeats, especially four in a row in the league, is not acceptable," said coach Bruno Genesio after Sunday's loss at the Stade Velodrome.
“We know that every Ligue 1 match is difficult and when you can pick up points against very good teams, that gives you confidence and also allows you to build on that.
"In the last few matches, we haven't got what we deserved, but we also haven't done enough to deserve better,” he added.
Genesio, who arrived at the start of the season from Lille, will use the next three weeks during the international window to assess the situation.
"There is no question of resigning," he told reporters.
"I'll take stock with the management, with my staff, and with the players, because for now what matters to me is helping the team improve.

“On the team's spirit and commitment, I don't have much to criticise since the start of the season. We simply have to do better in our own penalty area. We're conceding far too many avoidable goals,” Genesio added
Marseille, who finished fifth last season, have three points from their opening five league games and suffered a 4-1 loss at Besiktas in the opening Europa League fixture last week.
Their next match is a visit to Troyes on Oct 11 before hosting Greece’s Olympiakos four days later.
ce189e2f300115b8: NAGOYA: A sport once banned in much of the United States and famously decried as "human cockfighting" by a high-profile politician is making an ambitious play for the Olympics.
Mixed Martial Arts, better known as MMA, is making its Asian Games debut this week in Japan - a milestone that fighters and organisers hope will one day lead to an even bigger prize.
Galastein Tan, director general of the Federation of International Mixed Martial Arts, said being at the Asian Games was "a big step".
"As for any sport, the inclusion in the continental games is critical," he told AFP in Nagoya.

"Obviously the inclusion means that you already have a good governance structure, you have enough members, athletes to be able to compete, your ruleset, your officials are ready and therefore it is a significant one."
At a compact gym akin to a school sports hall, men and women scrap it out in separate categories in front of a modest but enthusiastic crowd.
Many of the competitors are from countries with proud histories in fighting sports - Thailand, Kazakhstan, the Philippines and hosts Japan to name a few.
Inspiring a generation
For fans of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), the MMA promoter synonymous with the sport, there is one immediate difference.
In UFC, which in June held an event on the South Lawn of the White House, the rough and tumble takes place inside a caged octagon.
At the Asian Games competitors do battle on a white and grey mat, but they are not fenced in.
For martial artists used to fighting in a cage, this takes some adapting to - a fence "does not really align with Olympic values", said Tan.
Getting everyone to agree on the rules of the competition, including what moves are allowed, is one major obstacle to MMA being at the Olympics.
Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon, who is guaranteed to win at least a silver medal, said that Asian Games and Olympic recognition will encourage a generation to take up the sport.
"I think it will grow the talent pool a lot," she said.
"It will encourage more children and teenagers to take up the sport and take it seriously.
"Because now there's a clear pathway, right? You can join a national team, the next step you can go to the Olympics."
'We are ready'
MMA is not the only sport debuting at Asia's premier sporting event and hoping one day to get into the Olympics.
So too is teqball - roughly a crossover between football and table tennis - and there is also the fast-growing racquet sport of padel.
It makes for a crowded field, and there are many other sports with Olympic ambitions.
Plenty of hard work and political lobbying lies ahead if MMA is to make it.
"We have been in talks with the IOC and other relevant stakeholders that have influence or decision on the recognition," said an upbeat Tan.
The sport does have Dana White in its corner - the UFC chief is openly supportive of Olympic inclusion.
Of the other issues on the long path to Olympic recognition there is a perception in the eyes of some that MMA is too violent.
Still, driven by the phenomenal success of the UFC, MMA is now mainstream - a far cry from the 1990s when US senator John McCain likened the early version of the sport to cockfighting.
Getting the whole of MMA to coalesce around one governing body is also essential if an Olympic place is to one day come.
Los Angeles in 2028 is too soon, and then comes Brisbane four years later.
"Nothing is impossible," said Tan.
"We hope that MMA is a sport that the Olympics finds relevance to and the ability to connect with both adults and also the youth.
"(It is) a sport which has global appeal and a sport that is ready and capable of fitting into a major Games schedule.
"So if the IOC or LA28 comes and say, MMA, would you like to be in as a medal sport or demo sport, we are ready."
3e986b29c8fc1c71: SHAH ALAM: Bekas pengurus pemasaran Pertubuhan Peladang Kawasan (PPK) Bernam Jaya mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Sesyen di sini hari ini, atas 27 pertuduhan menggunakan dokumen palsu berkaitan urusan pembelian sawit bernilai lebih RM500,000.

Malaysia will also be represented in PUBG Mobile, where players were selected based on merit and performances in professional competitions.

Naim also apologised to supporters over the recent controversy involving veteran MLBB player Zul Hisham Noor, who was left out of the final Asian Games line-up.

Zul Hisham, known as Xorn, was initially a substitute and played a key role in Malaysia's 2-1 win over Indonesia during the Southeast Asian qualifier, but later revealed that he learned of his removal through WhatsApp.
He has since met Naim to clear up the misunderstandings surrounding the incident.
"When we give the players this responsibility, we, as fans, also have a responsibility to continue giving the team our full support wherever they compete," said Naim.
Meanwhile, MPL Malaysia Season 18 has begun a two-week break to accommodate the Asian Games and will resume on Oct 8.
Week Six ended with Team Rey defeating SRG 2-1 on Sunday, while Bigetron Malaysia edged Invictus Gaming by the same score.
On Saturday, Team Vamos swept Bigetron Malaysia 2-0, Invictus Gaming beat RRQ Tora 2-1, and SRG downed All Combo Esports 2-0.
Team Rey opened the week with a 2-1 win over Team Flash on Friday, while Team Vamos defeated RRQ Tora 2-1.
The Asian Games esports competition begins at the Aichi Sky Expo centre on Wednesday.
3c3f9af68b4473fa: PETALING JAYA: Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chief Ab Rauf Yusoh has asked parties interested in striking up an alliance with the coalition for the Melaka polls to be patient, as Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders press BN for a decision.
He urged them against discussing the matter on social media, saying this could create a negative perception of the parties involved, Bernama reported.
"There is no need for us to negotiate through social media. We will issue official letters to all parties, inviting them to submit proposals on how they could become BN’s best strategic partner.
"These proposals will then be presented at all levels for a decision," the Melaka chief minister said.
Rauf reiterated that BN was open to talks with all parties for a Melaka election agreement. "We are neither closing the door completely nor opening it wide for negotiations."
Last night, PH election director Amirudin Shari urged BN to reveal whether it was interested in an alliance for the Melaka state election.
The PKR vice-president said PH had no issues if BN decided not to form an alliance, but that a decision should be made soon so that PH could prepare accordingly.
Similarly, Melaka Wawasan chief Rahim Thamby Chik said PN would go solo in all 28 seats in Melaka if it failed to reach an agreement with BN.
9d449d84364bed26: PETALING JAYA: PAS treasurer-general Iskandar Abdul Samad has advised party members to prioritise their responsibilities to the party before contributing to the fund to help settle former prime minister Najib Razak's RM50 million fine.
Iskandar said PAS members should prioritise contributing to the fund to build the Islamic party's new headquarters near Putrajaya, which would also cost about RM50 million.
He added that PAS members should contribute to the party's "Infaq Istiqamah" monthly donation scheme and their relevant local divisions and branches.
"As PAS treasurer-general, I would definitely want PAS members to prioritise their responsibilities (to the party)," he told FMT.
Iskandar also said he believed that Umno supporters alone would be able to cover the amount required.
He was asked if PAS would contribute to the fund launched by Umno to help Najib pay the RM50 million fine as part of his conditional pardon to serve the remainder of his jail term under house arrest.
PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man previously said the party was leaving it to members to decide whether to contribute to Najib's fund.
afc08b8361556f46: KUALA LUMPUR: A cancer-stricken former Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) radiology technician has threatened to sue the hospital over alleged SOP breaches in the department if an amicable settlement is not reached.

Lawyer Wan Azmir Wan Majid, representing Nur Fauzia Abdul Razak who is battling stage 4 Hodgkin lymphoma, said his client would file a negligence suit or initiate judicial discovery proceedings against UMMC if no discussions are held.
"If there is no meeting held between Fauzia and UMMC, then we have no choice but to litigate this matter.
"Our next action is either to push for a cause of action, filing for negligence straight away, or to go for a discovery action against UMMC," Wan Azmir told reporters at a press conference.
In April, Fauzia claimed that years after the hospital installed a PET-CT machine, three staff members suffered from cancer, while another four were suffering from thyroid-related diseases.
All seven were attached to the radiology department, she claimed.
UMMC denied the allegations, saying its PET-CT machine was always operated according to strict security procedures, with the level of radiation exposure under control and according to set standards.

The hospital also said staff members who worked with the machine were required to be equipped with personal dosimeters, and official records showed that each person’s level of exposure to radiation was far lower than the gazetted dose.
The health ministry cleared UMMC of allegations of SOP breaches after a probe of the matter.

A coalition of civil society groups comprising Secretariat Reformasi Institusi Pendidikan Tinggi, Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia and Himpunan Advokasi Rakyat Malaysia is nevertheless urging Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to establish a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) into the matter.
The coalition wants the RCI to investigate alleged safety non-compliance and the manipulation of personal radiation exposure records at the hospital.
14c4d465cdb8d574: KUALA LUMPUR: Moto3 rider Hakim Danish Ramli admitted that pushing too hard proved costly at the Austrian Grand Prix, but took heart from his determined fightback to finish ninth on Sunday.
The Malaysian rider made an encouraging start after lining up 15th at the Red Bull Ring, gaining several positions early on.
However, Hakim lost ground after making several mistakes midway through the race.
"I made a good start and tried to push the bike to its maximum, which allowed me to gain several positions in the early stages," said Hakim on Monday.
"However, midway through the race, I struggled a little as I was pushing too hard and made a few mistakes.
"That caused me to lose some positions and drop back down the field."
Instead of allowing the setback to derail his race, Hakim regrouped and recovered strongly over the closing laps.
The AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider felt increasingly comfortable on his bike as the race progressed and worked his way back into the top 10.
"Towards the end of the race, I worked hard to fight back and pushed to overtake several riders ahead of me," the 19-year-old added.
"My feeling with the bike also improved during the closing stages.
"I would like to thank the team for all their hard work throughout the weekend."
Hakim eventually crossed the line in ninth, edging Japanese teammate Ryusei Yamanaka at the finish.
The seven points lifted him to seventh in the riders' standings with 101 points.
It also provided a positive conclusion to a challenging weekend after Hakim crashed on his warm-up lap in Q2 and qualified 15th.
With the European round completed, Hakim is eager to carry the lessons and momentum from Austria into the upcoming Asian leg of the season.
"I'm really looking forward to the next race in Asia, especially in Japan, and I'm determined to achieve an even stronger result," he said.
The next Moto3 race will be on Oct 4 at the Twin Ring Motegi circuit in Japan.
5c1c0e3e1f720970: PETALING JAYA: Harga elektrik berkemungkinan akan terus meningkat dalam tempoh lima tahun akan datang berikutan Malaysia mengalami kekurangan bekalan gas domestik ketika sedang menamatkan penggunaan loji jana kuasa arang batu, kata Rafizi Ramli.
Bekas menteri ekonomi itu berkata isu berkenaan bukan hanya mengenai TNB atau bil elektrik, sebaliknya cabaran keselamatan tenaga yang mendesak.
"Ini bukan sekadar masalah TNB. Ini adalah masalah negara," katanya dalam satu episod audio siar Yang Berhenti Menteri baru-baru ini.
Rafizi berkata sistem penjanaan elektrik Malaysia direka beberapa dekad lalu ketika negara mempunyai bekalan gas yang banyak.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, bekalan gas domestik di Semenanjung Malaysia kini semakin tidak mencukupi, menyebabkan negara terpaksa meningkatkan kebergantungan kepada import gas asli cecair (LNG).

Katanya, kesannya sudah dapat dilihat pada harga gas, dengan harga gas Tahap 2 melonjak daripada paras rujukan kira-kira RM46 bagi setiap juta unit terma British (MMBtu) kepada antara RM70 hingga RM80 setiap MMBtu susulan gangguan di sekitar Selat Hormuz.

Menurut Rafizi, kenaikan harga yang mendadak itu menunjukkan bekalan gas domestik tidak mencukupi untuk memenuhi permintaan sektor elektrik, walaupun pada kadar sekitar 800 juta kaki padu piawai sehari.
“Malaysia perlu mengimport gas. Ini bermakna keseimbangan bekalan gas sudah menjadi masalah,” katanya.
Rafizi berkata langkah kerajaan baru-baru ini untuk mengurangkan beban bil elektrik tidak seharusnya dilihat sebagai penyelesaian kekal.
Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim baru-baru ini mengumumkan perlindungan bil elektrik bagi pengguna domestik akan diperluas daripada 600kWh kepada 800kWh sebulan mulai bulan ini hingga 31 Dis.
Di bawah langkah itu, pengguna domestik yang menggunakan sehingga 800kWh sebulan akan dikecualikan daripada Pelarasan Bahan Api Automatik (AFA), caj runcit serta cukai jualan dan perkhidmatan.

Bagaimanapun, Rafizi memberi amaran bahawa masalah asas itu akan menjadi lebih serius apabila pengeluaran gas asli domestik terus merosot, menyebabkan Malaysia semakin bergantung kepada import bagi memenuhi permintaan.
Bekalan elektrik di Semenanjung Malaysia bergantung terutamanya kepada tiga sumber, iaitu arang batu, gas dan tenaga boleh baharu.
Data terkini menunjukkan arang batu menyumbang kira-kira 57.9% daripada penjanaan elektrik, diikuti gas sebanyak 34.9%, manakala hidro dan solar masing-masing menyumbang 4.7% dan 2.5%.
Rafizi berkata Malaysia tidak boleh terus bergantung kepada arang batu sebagai penyelesaian jangka panjang, sambil menyatakan komitmen negara untuk mencapai pelepasan sifar bersih menjelang 2050.

Katanya, penjanaan elektrik berintensiti karbon tinggi juga boleh menyebabkan pengeksport Malaysia dikenakan cukai karbon di pasaran seperti Eropah, Jepun dan Korea Selatan, sekali gus menjejaskan daya saing mereka di pasaran global.

Pada masa sama, katanya, tenaga solar tidak boleh dikembangkan dengan cukup pantas untuk menggantikan arang batu sepenuhnya kerana kekangan berkaitan tanah, penyimpanan bateri, pembiayaan dan pelaksanaan sistem solar atas bumbung yang perlahan.
“Kita tidak boleh menjadikan seluruh negara sebagai ladang solar. Kita masih memerlukan tanah untuk penanaman padi, kelapa sawit dan kegunaan lain,” katanya.
Amaran itu dibuat ketika kerajaan turut mengkaji potensi tenaga nuklear dalam campuran tenaga Malaysia pada masa depan.

Timbalan Perdana Menteri Fadillah Yusof berkata pada Mac bahawa MyPOWER Corporation Malaysia sedang menjalankan penilaian menyeluruh terhadap potensi program tenaga nuklear Malaysia, meliputi pembangunan dasar, rangka kerja perundangan dan kawal selia, kebolehlaksanaan projek, penyertaan industri, penglibatan pihak berkepentingan serta pembangunan modal insan.
Rafizi berkata gas sepatutnya berperanan sebagai bahan api peralihan ketika Malaysia meningkatkan penggunaan tenaga boleh baharu dan mengurangkan kebergantungan kepada arang batu secara berperingkat.
Namun, katanya, keadaan itu menimbulkan percanggahan kerana Malaysia tidak mempunyai bekalan gas domestik yang mencukupi.

Rafizi berkata kebergantungan yang lebih besar kepada LNG import akan menyebabkan aliran keluar tunai meningkat kerana pembelian dibuat dalam dolar AS, sekali gus memberi tekanan kepada ringgit sekiranya Malaysia perlu membelanjakan berbilion ringgit setiap tahun untuk mendapatkan bekalan gas import.

Beliau memberi amaran bahawa kebergantungan kepada gas import juga akan melemahkan kedaulatan tenaga Malaysia, dengan mengambil contoh kebergantungan Eropah kepada gas murah dari Rusia sebelum perang Rusia-Ukraine.
“Kita sudah melihat apa yang berlaku kepada negara-negara Eropah apabila mereka terlalu bergantung kepada gas murah dari Rusia,” katanya.
Rafizi berkata beban itu akhirnya akan ditanggung pengguna kerana kerajaan tidak boleh selama-lamanya memberikan subsidi bagi menampung kos elektrik.
Katanya, mekanisme AFA perlu difahami dalam konteks yang lebih luas kerana bil elektrik berkemungkinan semakin terdedah kepada perubahan harga bahan api dan kadar pertukaran asing.

Rafizi berkata kekurangan gas, peningkatan kos import dan peralihan daripada arang batu bermakna tarif elektrik akan terus berada di bawah tekanan melainkan Malaysia mempercepatkan pembangunan tenaga boleh baharu dan menangani masalah keseimbangan bekalan gas negara dalam jangka panjang.
fa2023257da454ad: SEOUL, Sept 21 — BTS member Jungkook has reached another streaming milestone after Standing Next to You surpassed 500 million plays on YouTube Music.

The Korea Herald reported that the track is now the fourth Jungkook song to cross the mark on the platform, following Seven featuring Latto, 3D featuring Jack Harlow and his collaboration with Charlie Puth, Left and Right.
Standing Next to You, the main track from Jungkook’s debut solo album Golden, also recorded strong international chart performances after its release.
The retro-funk song opened at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped both the Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. US charts, while reaching No. 6 on the UK Official Singles Top 100.

Jungkook returned to South Korea on Monday after BTS performed four songs at the iHeartRadio Music Festival in Las Vegas.
The appearance marked the septet’s first time performing at the festival since 2020.
1548123c6216489c: MELAKA, Sept 21 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has advised parties interested in collaborating with the coalition in the upcoming state election not to negotiate such matters via social media.
